Hon'ble Arun Kumar Singh Deshwal,J.
1.

Sri Dhananjay Kumar, Advocate has filed Vakalatnama on behalf of opposite party no.2 today in
the Court, which is taken on record.

2. Heard Sri Rajesh Kumar Singh, learned counsel for the applicants, .Sri Dhananjay Kumar,
learned counsel for opposite party No.2 and learned A.G.A. for the State.

3. The instant application has been filed to quash impugned charge sheet no. 288/20 dated 10.09.2020 along with cognizance/summoning order dated 25.01.2021 passed by Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Court No.1, Agra in Case No. 1594 of 2021 (State Vs. Chand and others) arising out of Case Crime No. 235 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 452, 504, 506, 427 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P.Act, P.S. Malpura, District Agra.

sentences.text:
4. Learned counsel for the applicants submits that dispute between the parties is matrimonial in Chand And 6 Others vs State Of U.P. And Another on 5 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/36682266/
1 nature and both the parties have settled their dispute amicably and entered into a written compromise dated 21.09.2024 annexed as Annexure SA-3 to the supplementary affidavit.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It has been requested that the impugned proceedings may be quashed on the basis of compromise.
5. Though learned counsel for opposite party No.2 did not dispute the above fact, learned AGA states that the impugned proceeding cannot be quashed until the aforesaid compromise is verified.
6. In view of the above, the applicants are directed to file the original deed of compromise before the court below within a period of 15 days from today.

7. In case such a compromise is filed by the applicants, the court below will verify the said compromise after summoning the parties within a period of two months from the date of filing the compromise and after verification, the court below will dispose of the impugned proceeding in accordance with law.
8. For a period of two and a half months or till verification of compromise, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicants in the aforesaid case.
9. However, the parties are at liberty to file a fresh application under Section 528 BNSS to quash the impugned proceeding on the basis of verified copy of compromise, if need arises.
10. With the aforesaid direction, the present application is disposed of.
